Gamer: original adult man with short dark wavy hair, round glasses and a dark blue work jacket over a light gray shirt, screen-right. These are original adult anthology interviewees, not canonical recurring characters or real-person likenesses.

The gamer indicates its worn corner once with an open empty palm, then briefly gestures toward his own chest. Both hands remain separate and anatomically clear.

The reporter remains serious until the last word, looks at the worn box, looks back at him, tries to hold her smile and breaks into a caused audible laugh. He notices her reaction and joins later. The crowd starts after the two leads, with different reactions and timing.

The laugh is clearly visible and AUDIBLE: microphone lowers to waist, eyes squeeze, head tips back briefly, then a small forward lean with two uneven shoulder bounces and one hand against the abdomen. The gamer holds a straight face for a short recognition beat, then cracks into an amused grin and joins with a shorter irregular voiced laugh. Nearby supporters react later and differently; no synchronized mechanical swaying. Both catch their breath and exchange an amused look. Laughter must have a cause in this exchange. Keep feet planted, prop supported and boards motionless. No frozen faces, talking-mouth-only acting, anticipation before the joke, flat monotone or tiny polite chuckle.

Essa placa já trabalhou mais que eu!</d> No repeated words or additional utterances. Reporter reacts only after the last word, with a short recognition beat, an unsuccessful attempt to hold a smile, microphone lowered below the mouth, then a clear AUDIBLE warm voiced belly laugh. Eyes close, shoulders bounce twice unevenly, body leans forward briefly and recovers. Gamer joins later with a shorter clearly audible spontaneous laugh. The crowd reacts after the two leads, with different timing, never synchronized swaying. Laughing is nonverbal: no invented words, babble or extra syllables. Let the uneven voiced laughing reaction play from 8.0 to 13.2 seconds, followed by a natural breath and recovery through 15 seconds. No words during laughter or recovery.

One static continuous shot, normal speed, no cuts or zoom. Only specified exact dialogue tags contain spoken words. Laughter is native in-scene nonverbal voiced laughter with irregular breaths, not extra syllables or words. No canned laugh track, narrator, music, subtitles, logos, watermarks or added verbal remarks. Keep background street ambience soft under dialogue and laughter.
